atoms.claim: Realtime task dispatch has a mechanical two-step human-intent gate: frank_auftrag_stellen first records a proposal, then dispatches only after an exact normalized text match, bestaetigt=true, at least one new server-transcribed user utterance, no keyword contradiction, and a <=300s proposal age.

Realtime function-call execution retains the host/model call_id for function_call_output and clears pending tool calls on barge-in/cancelled turns, preventing an interrupted response's queued call from being executed later.

frank_erinnerung_schreiben is dispatched directly to stern.gespraech_erinnerung_schreiben without the task dispatcher's two-step human confirmation. The stern writer inserts subject/value into the bounded gespraech_erinnerung table in the same unified.db and commits immediately.

The realtime memory writer is intentionally bounded to a dedicated gespraech_erinnerung table and explicitly does not write durable_memory, preserving the donor's single durable_memory writer invariant. Therefore this finding is a mutation-intent inconsistency, not evidence that the realtime model has arbitrary UnifiedDB write access.

VoiceSessionCapsule is refreshed from live sources but _response_erstellen composes per-response instructions from _instruktion(self._zustandstext) plus optional hint; no inspected path serializes self.capsule into those instructions.
When PresenceBridge data is unavailable in inspected realtime paths, donor fallback behavior can set user_present=True rather than preserving UNKNOWN/None.

hypotheses.claim: Frankenstein 2.0 will be safer and easier to reason about if every mutating Realtime function call is classified by mutation type and passes an explicit HumanIntentDecision before any canonical-state mutation or EffectRequest, while EffectGate remains a separate deterministic authority for external effects.
hypotheses.falsifier: A complete source audit proves every mutating Realtime path already receives equivalent mechanically bound user-intent admission before commit/dispatch, with tests covering memory writes, task dispatch, configuration/state writes, cancellation and replay.

hypotheses.claim: The donor's call_id lifecycle is a useful predecessor for the immutable per-call invocation identity required by the current EffectDecision design, but it is not sufficient until that identity remains bound across Realtime dispatch, host executor, EffectGate/Journal and result re-entry.
hypotheses.falsifier: Executable end-to-end evidence shows a different immutable identity already provides collision-free binding across all those boundaries and call_id is intentionally discarded without loss.

counterhypotheses.claim: Immediate bounded conversational-memory writes may be an intentionally low-risk mutation class that should not require the same explicit confirmation UX as external task execution.
counterhypotheses.discriminator: Define mutation classes and user-expectation policy, then test whether memory writes are always semantically recoverable/reversible and whether model-misheard or third-party speech can create unwanted durable entries.

counterhypotheses.claim: VoiceSessionCapsule may influence response behavior indirectly through another path not covered by the inspected spans.
counterhypotheses.discriminator: Search all reads/serializations of self.capsule/capsule_quelle and run a field lesion/shuffle test against emitted response.instructions before declaring the capsule behaviorally disconnected.

contradictions.claim_a: Task execution is treated as requiring a mechanically evidenced second human utterance and explicit confirmation before dispatch.
contradictions.claim_b: A model-issued conversational-memory mutation commits immediately to a durable UnifiedDB table without the same confirmation mechanism.
contradictions.note: Do not collapse this into an external-effect bypass claim; the memory table is a bounded internal state surface. The unresolved issue is which mutation classes require which human-intent evidence and how that decision binds to invocation identity.

critical_unknowns: Whether any additional mutating Realtime tools or indirect configuration writers exist outside the inspected dispatch table.
Whether product policy intends low-risk reversible memory writes to be implicitly authorized by normal conversation, or requires explicit confirmation/provenance tagging.
Whether VoiceSessionCapsule is serialized by an uninspected indirect path before websocket response.create.
Runtime behavior was not re-executed in this Triggerword-5 pass; all credit is source-forensics only.
recommended_next_spans: Audit the complete TOOLS declaration and every _tool_ausfuehren mutating branch, then classify READ_ONLY / EPHEMERAL_STATE / CANONICAL_INTERNAL_MUTATION / EXTERNAL_EFFECT_REQUEST / SESSION_CONTROL.
Trace call_id from Realtime response.output_item.done through every bridge to Claude Code/host execution and prove where immutable identity is lost or preserved.
Search all self.capsule and capsule_quelle consumers to close the VoiceSessionCapsule conditioning contradiction with direct source evidence.
